parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Lecturer: Thank you all for coming here today to hear about the Moa, a kind of animal which has been extinct for a long time. Well first of all we look at what the Moa are. The Moa are nine species of flightless birds endemic to New Zealand. They were the dominant herbivores in New Zealand's forest, shrubland and subalpine ecosystems for thousands of years, but around 500 years ago they all went extinct. When I mention extinct animals during ancient times you may immediately think of dinosaurs which disappeared around 66 million years ago. Fossils of dinosaurs which we use to study are large in number but not many of those of Moa remain, though both animals appeal to people today so the Moas sound more mysterious now.

Student: But sir I've got a question about these flightless birds. How can we distinguish them from other birds?

Lecturer: That's a good question. Birds are commonly characterized by being warm-blooded, having feathers and wings, usually capable of flight and laying eggs. While a flightless Moa, until their extinction, were the largest birds in the world. Their heads are relatively small in relation to their bodies and they are the only wingless birds lacking even the vestigial wings and substantial tailbones in their family.

Student: That's impressive, but were they born to be like that? I mean when they were chicks?

Lecturer: Yes, absolutely. So let's move on to the chicks. The eggs of Moa were laid in nests and incubated for about 2 months. The chicks would be well-developed upon hatching and probably would be able to leave the nests to feed on their own almost immediately.

Student: I've heard that the male Moa are thought to have incubated the eggs, is that true?

Lecturer: I think there is a possibility for that. I've read somewhere that the sex specific DNA recovered from the outer surfaces of eggshells suggested that these eggs were likely to have been hatched by the male, but we still need to consult more.

Student: But I have a question. There has been some occasional speculation that the Moa was still alive because someone said they had caught sight of them in New Zealand in the late 19th century or even the 20th. Do you think it's possible?

Lecturer: I'm not amazed by that since that kind of thing has been claimed several times, but I find it funny because no reliable evidence of Moa tracks has ever been found and experts still contend that Moa survival is extremely unlikely.

Student: So what was the reason for the Moa's extinction? I wonder if it was global warming or some other factors related to their living environment.

Lecturer: Well before the arrival of human settlers in New Zealand the Moa's only predator was the massive Haast's Eagle. Then the Maori arrived sometime before CE 1300 and all Moa were soon driven to extinction by hunting. What a horrible thing.

Lecturer: All right now let's look at the features of some species of Moa. The South Island Giant Moa may have been the tallest birds ever known and the second tallest of the nine Moa species is the North Island Giant Moa, with the females being markedly larger than males both in weight and height.

Student: And I've heard that the smallest of the Moa birds are the Coastal Moa, is that right?

Lecturer: Yes you were right. And have you heard about any other kind of Moa before?

Student: I know the Crested Moa. The eggs they laid may be larger than others as they mainly lived in the remote interior of the southern island. Their fossils are rare or absent in archaeological sites and no egg remains have yet been identified.

Student: Are there any species of Moa that have got more fossils?

Lecturer: Yes of course. A considerable amount of remains of the Stout-legged Moa exist due to the well-preserved properties of their habitat. Their skulls reveal relatively bad vision, a good sense of smell and a very short bill. Then there is the Eastern Moa. They were remarkable in having very long and narrow windpipes which probably enabled them to make louder, more resonant calls than those of other Moa and had the greatest vocal abilities. So they could communicate when they could not see each other in the forest or at night. They used a range of senses apart from sound in their search for food such as their sense of smell and vision.

questions.question: What is the thing that makes the Moa similar to dinosaur?

analyses.content: 讲师提到虽然恐鸟化石不多，但恐鸟和恐龙这两种动物如今都吸引着人们（appeal to people today），对应选项 A 的“公众感兴趣”。
Lecturer: Fossils of dinosaurs which we use to study are large in number but not many of those of Moa remain, though both animals appeal to people today so the Moas sound more mysterious now.
不要听到 dinosaur 就选 B（灭绝时间），录音明确说了恐龙灭绝于6600万年前，而恐鸟是500年前，两者时间完全不同；也不要选 C，录音说恐鸟的化石并不多（not many）。

questions.question: What is the difference between Moa and other birds?

analyses.content: Lecturer: Their heads are relatively small in relation to their bodies and they are the only wingless birds lacking even the vestigial wings and substantial tailbones in their family.
虽然提到了头比较小（relatively small），但这是描述特征，不是与其他鸟类区分的“唯一（only）”决定性差异，区分点在于完全无翅。
讲师强调恐鸟是唯一一种连退化翅膀（vestigial wings）都没有的无翼鸟，也就是完全没有翅膀骨头。

options.optionContent: They never return to the nests.

options.optionContent: Most of them die within two months after birth.

options.optionContent: They can find food by themselves.

questions.question: What’s the special feature of their chicks?

analyses.content: Lecturer: The eggs of Moa were laid in nests and incubated for about 2 months. The chicks would be well-developed upon hatching and probably would be able to leave the nests to feed on their own almost immediately.
听到 "leave the nests" 不要想当然选 A（从不回巢），录音只说了离巢觅食，没说不回来；B 选项的“两个月”是孵化期，不是存活期。
讲师说小恐鸟孵化后发育良好，几乎可以立刻离开巢穴去自己觅食（feed on their own），对应选项 C。

questions.question: What is the tutor’s opinion on male hatching the eggs?

analyses.content: Student: I've heard that the male Moa are thought to have incubated the eggs, is that true? Lecturer: I think there is a possibility for that. ...suggested that these eggs were likely to have been hatched by the male, but we still need to consult more.
讲师最后补充说“还需要参考更多资料（still need to consult more）”，说明还没有达到 C 选项那样“完全确定（certainty）”的程度，但也绝不是 A 选项的“怀疑”。
针对雄性孵蛋的说法，讲师说“认为有这个可能性”（think there is a possibility），并且 DNA 证据也表明“likely”（很可能）。

questions.question: What is the male student’s response after hearing some people see a Moa recently?

analyses.content: Student: ...Do you think it's possible? Lecturer: I'm not amazed by that since that kind of thing has been claimed several times, but I find it funny because no reliable evidence of Moa tracks has ever been found...
听到 "I'm not amazed" 就可以排除 A（惊讶），讲师的态度是觉得这种传闻很可笑，而不是担心或惊讶。
注意：题目问的是 male student 的反应，但根据答案 C 和录音内容，这里实际考查的是讲师（回答者）对“有人目击恐鸟”这件事的态度。 讲师说他觉得这事“很滑稽/好笑”（I find it funny），因为没有可靠证据，专家认为不可能。

questions.question: Why did the Moa become extinct?

analyses.content: 讲师说毛利人（Maori）到达新西兰后，恐鸟很快因为狩猎（hunting）而灭绝，狩猎属于人类干预。
Lecturer: Well before the arrival of human settlers in New Zealand... Then the Maori arrived sometime before CE 1300 and all Moa were soon driven to extinction by hunting.
讲师提到了“arrival of human settlers”，所以不是 A（气候变化）或 C（与其他动物竞争），虽然提到了鹰（Eagle），那是人类到来之前的捕食者，不是灭绝原因。

27 the North Island Giant Moa

30 the Eastern Moa

analyses.content: Lecturer: ...the second tallest of the nine Moa species is the North Island Giant Moa, with the females being markedly larger than males both in weight and height.
听到 "tallest birds" 确定是关于身高的描述，重点在于后面提到的性别差异（females larger）。
录音中提到该物种的雌性在体重和身高上都明显比雄性大（markedly larger than males），对应选项 A。
Student: I know the Crested Moa... Their fossils are rare or absent in archaeological sites and no egg remains have yet been identified.
不要听到 eggs 就选 C，这里说的是 "no egg remains have yet been identified"（没发现蛋的遗骸），而不是蛋很大。
录音说这种恐鸟的化石很稀少或在遗址中缺失（fossils are rare or absent），对应选项 B（留下的化石较少）。
Lecturer: A considerable amount of remains of the Stout-legged Moa exist... Their skulls reveal relatively bad vision, a good sense of smell and a very short bill.
这一题是直接的同义替换，bad vision = poor eyesight，只要抓住了 vision 这个词就不容易错。
录音提到它们的头骨显示视力相对较差（relatively bad vision），直接对应选项 F。

Lecturer: Then there is the Eastern Moa. They were remarkable in having very long and narrow windpipes which probably enabled them to make louder, more resonant calls than those of other Moa and had the greatest vocal abilities.
虽然录音后面提到了 communication（交流）和 smell/vision（嗅觉/视觉），但最突出、描述最多的特征是它的声音能力。
录音说这种恐鸟有很长很窄的气管，能发出更响亮、更共鸣的叫声（louder, more resonant calls），拥有最强的发声能力（greatest vocal abilities）。

groups.description: Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A-F.
